parts: Rohan has joined the company two years ago,
and since then he has worked in
now supervises a team of five clerks.
items.explanation: A finished time expression such as “two years ago” needs the simple past: “Rohan joined the company two years ago”, not “has joined”.

parts: One of the most useful features
of this mobile application are that
items.explanation: The subject is the singular pronoun “One”, not “features”, so “are” should be “is”.

parts: of its employees, who have always
items.explanation: Dependent preposition: “committed” is followed by “to”, so “committed for delivering” should be “committed to delivering”.
Article choice depends on sound, not spelling: “university” begins with a consonant sound, so “an university” should be “a university”.
The sentence is correct: “Neither of” takes a singular verb, so “has submitted” and “has been postponed” are both right.

parts: from a distant city that evening.
items.explanation: Pronoun case: “My brother and me” is the subject of “went”, so the subject form is needed: “My brother and I went”.

sentences: The library have extended its opening hours so that students can study there until late in the evening.
The library has extended its opening hours so that students can studying there until late in the evening.
The library has extended its opening hours so that students can study there until late in the evening.
The library has extended its opening hours so that students can study there until late in a evening.
Students say that they now concentrate much more better in the evenings than they did at home.
items.explanation: The correct sentence has no fault. The others contain the plural verb “have” with the singular “library”, “can studying” instead of “can study”, “a evening” instead of “an evening”, and the double comparative “more better”.

parts: scheme from the head office and
items.explanation: “Information” is an uncountable noun and has no plural, so “several informations” is wrong; use “some information”.

parts: This new laptop is cheaper, and
it has a longer battery life,
items.explanation: “Heavier” is already a comparative, so “more heavier” is a double comparative and should be “heavier”.
The verb “performed” needs an adverb, not an adjective: “performed very well”, not “performed very good”.

sentences: Most customers prefers to shop online because they can compare prices easily and receive their orders at home.
Most customers prefer to shop online because they can compare prices easy and receive their orders at home.
Most customers prefer to shop online because they can compare prices easily and receiving their orders at home.
Most of customers prefer to shop online because they can compare prices easily and receive their orders at home.
Most customers prefer to shop online because they can compare prices easily and receive their orders at home.
items.explanation: The last sentence is the only one without a fault. The others contain “Most customers prefers”, the adjective “easy” for an adverb, “and receiving” breaking parallelism, and “Most of customers” instead of “Most customers” or “Most of the customers”.

parts: The bank manager said that he
items.explanation: “Unless” already means “if ... not”, so adding “not” makes a double negative: “unless the applicant submitted all the required documents”.

parts: they must to attach a recent photograph.
items.explanation: A modal verb is followed by the bare infinitive, so “must to attach” should be “must attach”.

parts: Ravi did not knew the answer
to the last question, so he
the concept again after the class was over.
items.explanation: After “did not” the base form of the verb is used, so “did not knew” should be “did not know”.

parts: condition of the main road and
has promised to repair it soon.
items.explanation: “Complaints” is a plural countable noun, so it takes “many”, not “much”.

sentences: The meeting, which began at ten o'clock, lasted since almost three hours because several important issues had to be discussed.
The meeting, which began at ten o'clock, lasted for almost three hours because several important issues had to be discussed.
The meeting, which began at ten o'clock, lasted for almost three hour because several important issues had to be discussed.
The meeting, which began at ten o'clock, lasted for almost three hours because of several important issues had to be discussed.
The meeting, which began at ten o'clock, lasted for almost three hours because several important issues had to be discussing.
items.explanation: The correct sentence uses “for” with a period of time and a complete “because” clause. The others contain “lasted since”, “three hour”, “because of” before a full clause, and the faulty passive “to be discussing”.

parts: budget cuts were a shock to everyone.
items.explanation: “News” is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb, and it is the subject here, so “were a shock” should be “was a shock”.

parts: because the bell was about to ring
and the next class was waiting outside.
items.explanation: The sentence is correct: “quickly” rightly modifies the verb “complete”, and “asked ... to complete” and the past tenses are used correctly.

parts: noon on Thursday, we will deliver
the goods to your office by
the evening and send you a confirmation message.
items.explanation: The sentence is correct: after “If” the present simple “arrives” is used for a future event, and “will deliver ... and send” is a consistent result clause.

sentences: Doctors advise that people should walk for at least thirty minutes every day to keep their hearts healthy.
Doctors advise people to walks for at least thirty minutes every day to keep their hearts healthy.
Doctors advises that people should walk for at least thirty minutes every day to keep their hearts healthy.
Doctors advise that people should walk during at least thirty minutes every day to keep their hearts healthy.
Doctors advise that people should walk for at least thirty minutes every day to keep their hearts healthily.
items.explanation: The first sentence is the only one without a fault. The others contain “to walks” (an infinitive needs the base verb), “Doctors advises”, “during at least thirty minutes” instead of “for”, and the adverb “healthily” where “keep ... healthy” needs an adjective.
